items.title: Transmuting Ordinary Materials into Treasure, Trained Through the Eight Mastery-Bases

items.zh: 若於草葉、牛糞、泥等，起於飲食、車乘、衣服、嚴飾資具、種種塗香、華鬘勝解，即隨勝解如實非餘。若於沙石、瓦礫等物，起於末尼、真珠、琉璃、螺貝、壁玉、珊瑚勝解，即隨勝解如實非餘。若於諸山、雪山王等起金勝解，即隨勝解如實非餘。若於一切起餘勝解，即隨勝解如實非餘。
items.en: If, regarding grass, leaves, dung, or mud, the resolute conviction is formed that these are food, a carriage, clothing, ornaments, fragrant incense, or garlands, they genuinely become exactly that. If, regarding sand, gravel, or rubble, the resolute conviction is formed that these are gemstones, pearls, or lapis lazuli, they genuinely become exactly that. If, regarding any mountain, even the great snow-capped king of mountains, the resolute conviction is formed that it is gold, it genuinely becomes gold.

items.title: Section: Transmuting a Being's Own Appearance — The Ghost Story That Dissolved a Monk's Attachment to Self

items.zh: 若於好色有情起惡色勝解，於惡色有情起好色勝解，於俱非有情起好色、惡色勝解，於俱有情起俱非勝解，即隨勝解如實非餘。如於好色、惡色，於具支節、不具支節，及肥瘦等，當知亦爾。
items.en: If, regarding a being of pleasing appearance, the resolute conviction is formed that they are of displeasing appearance — or the reverse — or regarding a being neither pleasing nor displeasing, that they are one or the other — or regarding a being who is both, that they are neither — it genuinely becomes exactly that. Just as with pleasing and displeasing appearance, so too with having complete or incomplete limbs, and with being stout or thin — it should be understood to hold the same way.

items.zh: 如是於餘所有自相可變色物起餘勝解，皆隨勝解一切轉變，如實非餘。是名轉變。

items.title: Coming and Going Without Obstruction, Folding Mount Sumeru Into an Atom, and Gathering Every Form Into One's Own Body

items.zh: 往來者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，隨其所樂，於諸牆壁、山石等中縱身往來，無有滯礙。廣說乃至往於梵世，乃至上至色究竟天，還來無礙。或復傍於無量無數三千大千世界，若往、若來皆無滯礙。
items.en: Coming and going: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, move their bodies freely through walls, mountains, and rock as they please, without any obstruction — extending even to journeying to the Brahmā realm and up to the highest form-realm heaven, returning without hindrance; or ranging across an immeasurable, uncountable number of great trichiliocosms, coming and going entirely without obstruction.

items.zh: 或運麁重四大種身，或於遠處作近勝解，或如意勢速疾往來。是名往來。
卷、舒者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，能卷一切雪山王等如一極微，舒一極微令如一切雪山王等。是名卷、舒。眾像入身者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，能以種種現前大眾，及以一切村邑、聚落、草木、叢林、諸山、大地一切色像內己身中，令諸大眾各各自知入其身內。
items.en: Contracting and expanding: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, can contract even the great snow-capped king of mountains until it is like a single mote of dust, and expand a single mote of dust until it is like the great snow-capped king of mountains. This is called contracting and expanding. Gathering forms into the body: ... they are able to gather the entire assembled crowd before them, along with every village, town, plant, forest, mountain, and expanse of earth, into their own body, causing everyone to directly know that they have entered within it.

items.title: Section: Going Forth in an Audience's Own Form — Two Stories of Mistaking a Bodhisattva for an Ordinary Being

items.zh: 同類往趣者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，或能往趣剎帝利眾，同其色類，如彼形量，似彼言音。彼若以此名如是義，亦即以此名如是義；彼不以此名如是義，亦不以此名如是義。然後為其演說正法，示現、教導、讚勵、慶慰。化事既終，欻然隱沒。
items.en: Going forth in the same form: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, are able to go among an assembly of kings and nobles in their same form, matching their stature and manner of speech ... and then expound the true teaching to them — showing, instructing, encouraging, and consoling. Once this work of transformation is complete, they suddenly vanish.

items.zh: 沒後時眾迭相顧言：不知沒者天耶？人耶？
items.en: After they vanish, the assembly looks at one another and asks: "Was the one who just disappeared a god, or a human being?"

items.title: Extending to Every Realm — The Full Ladder of Heavens

items.zh: 如能往趣剎帝利眾，如是往趣婆羅門眾、若沙門眾、若長者眾、若居士眾、四大王天、三十三天、夜摩天、覩史多天、樂變化天、他化自在天、梵眾天、梵先益天、大梵天、少光天、無量光天、光音天、少淨天、無量淨天、遍淨天、無雲天、福生天、廣果天、無煩天、無熱天、善現天、善見天、色究竟天，當知亦爾。
items.en: Just as one may go forth among an assembly of kings and nobles, so too among brahmins, ascetics, elders, and lay householders; among the Four Great Kings, the Thirty-Three, the Yāma heaven, the Tuṣita heaven, the heaven of delighting in creation, and the heaven of mastery over others' creations; among the Brahmā retinue heavens ... up to the highest form-realm heaven — it should be understood to hold the same way.

items.title: Appearing and Disappearing at Will, Free Accomplishment, and a Hierarchy of Restraining Power

items.zh: 隱、顯者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，於大眾前，百度、千度，或過於是，隱沒自身，復令顯現。是名隱、顯。所作自在者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，普於一切諸有情界往、來、住等所作事中，皆自在轉。令去即去，令住即住，令來即來，令語即語。
items.en: Concealing and revealing: ... before a great assembly, hundreds or thousands of times, or even more, they conceal themselves and then cause themselves to reappear. Free accomplishment: ... in every act of going, coming, staying, and so on, throughout the entire world of sentient beings, they act with complete freedom — whomever they cause to go goes, whomever they cause to stay stays, whomever they cause to come comes, and whomever they cause to speak speaks.

items.zh: 制他神通者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，能制伏他所現神通。如來神通普能制伏其餘一切具神通者所現神通，如其所欲，令事成辦。
items.en: Restraining others' miraculous power: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, are able to restrain the miraculous power displayed by others. A Tathāgata's own miraculous power is universally able to restrain the power displayed by every other possessor of miraculous power, accomplishing whatever is wished.

items.title: Section: The Ultimate Bodhisattva, and a Distinctive Teaching on Where Buddhahood Is Actually Attained

items.zh: 究竟菩薩一生所繫，或最後有所有神通，除諸如來、等類菩薩，悉能制伏其餘一切具神通者所現神通。諸餘菩薩所有神通，除入上地、等類菩薩，悉能制伏其餘一切具神通者所現神通。是名制他神通。
items.en: The miraculous power possessed by an ultimate bodhisattva — one bound to only one more rebirth, or one already in their final existence — is able to restrain the power displayed by every possessor of miraculous power other than the Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas of the same rank.

items.title: Bestowing Eloquence When Words Run Dry, and Memory When the Teaching Slips Away

items.zh: 能施辯才者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，若諸有情辯才窮盡，能與辯才。是名能施辯才。能施憶念者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，若諸有情於法失念，能與憶念。是名能施憶念。
items.en: Bestowing eloquence: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, are able to give eloquence to beings whose own eloquence has run out. This is called bestowing eloquence. Bestowing memory: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, are able to give memory back to beings who have lost their recollection of the teaching. This is called bestowing memory.

blocks.text: The rest of the transformations: the treatise describes them plainly, as what mastery of concentration makes possible.

"Grass, leaves, dung, or mud" become "food, carriages, clothing, ornaments"; sand and gravel become gems; "even the great snow mountain" becomes gold. A pleasing appearance can be made displeasing, or the reverse.

subs.head: Coming and going; contracting and expanding

blocks.text: "They move freely through walls, mountains, and rock", up to the highest form heaven. They "contract the great snow mountain until it is like a mote of dust, and expand a mote of dust until it is like the mountain".

"They go among an assembly of kings and nobles in their same form, matching their stature and speech", then expound the Dharma, "showing, instructing, encouraging, and consoling", and vanish. "The assembly asks: was that a god, or a human being?" The same among brahmins, ascetics, householders, and every heaven.

They conceal and reveal themselves "hundreds or thousands of times". They act with complete freedom. They can restrain others' powers; "a Tathāgata's power restrains all". The power of an "ultimate bodhisattva", one bound to one more birth or in the final existence, restrains all but a Buddha's.

"They give eloquence to beings whose eloquence has run out", and "give memory back to those who have lost their recollection of the teaching". Master Cháng Bǎi tells of a speaker who lost the thread halfway through a talk.

quiz.q: "Resolving that the snow-king mountain is gold." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: the mountain is earth and stone — now resolved as gold
quiz.why: "If, regarding any mountain, even the great snow-capped king of mountains, the resolute conviction is formed that it is gold, it genuinely becomes gold." Venerable Miào Jìng: this mountain is earth and stone; now one says it's gold — forming such a conviction.

quiz.q: Transmuting appearance "pleasing into displeasing." Both masters tell an Upagupta story — how do they differ?
options: Miào Jìng: Māra's beauties disrupting the assembly, turned old and ugly; Cháng Bǎi: the two ghosts swapping a body, stressing it was Upagupta's power
quiz.why: "If, regarding a being of pleasing appearance, the resolute conviction is formed that they are of displeasing appearance — or the reverse … it genuinely becomes exactly that." Venerable Miào Jìng: Venerable Upagupta used his power to turn those women into old crones — hideous. Master Cháng Bǎi, after the story of two ghosts swapping a body: of course this was Venerable Upagupta's power — how much more the buddhas and bodhisattvas!

quiz.q: "Coming and going without obstruction." What three kinds does Master Cháng Bǎi list?
options: through walls, vertically between realms, and horizontally across worlds
quiz.why: "Move their bodies freely through walls, mountains, and rock … up to the highest form-realm heaven … or ranging across an immeasurable number of great trichiliocosms." Master Cháng Bǎi: three kinds of mastery in coming and going — passing through walls, moving vertically between realms, and moving horizontally back and forth.

quiz.q: "Contracting the great snow-capped king of mountains into a mote of dust." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: shrinking a mountain as vast as the Himalayas to a dust mote
quiz.why: "Contracting and expanding: buddhas and bodhisattvas … can contract even the great snow-capped king of mountains until it is like a single mote of dust." Venerable Miào Jìng: this snow mountain, the Himalayas — very tall — can be shrunk into a single dust mote.

quiz.q: After matching their form, "showing, instructing, encouraging, consoling." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "showing"?
options: revealing the four kinds of reasoning — dependence, efficacy, proof, and natural law
quiz.why: "And then expound the true teaching to them — showing, instructing, encouraging, and consoling." Master Cháng Bǎi: revealing Buddhism's four kinds of reasoning — dependence, efficacy, valid proof, and the nature of things.

quiz.q: Free accomplishment: "令去即去, 令住即住" — rendered "going when they wish to go." Who goes, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: telling a being to go, it goes; to stay, it stays
quiz.why: "In every act of going, coming, staying … throughout the entire world of sentient beings, they act with complete freedom — going when they wish to go, staying when they wish to stay." Venerable Miào Jìng: tell that being to go and it goes; tell it to stay and it stays there. The English makes the bodhisattva the subject.

quiz.q: "An ultimate bodhisattva bound to one more rebirth." What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: one-life-left, like Maitreya in Tuṣita; Miào Jìng: the equal-awakening bodhisattva, one step from buddhahood
quiz.why: "An ultimate bodhisattva — one bound to only one more rebirth, or one already in their final existence." Master Cháng Bǎi: first, bound to one more life — one awaiting buddhahood, like Maitreya, whose life in Tuṣita is ending. Venerable Miào Jìng: what we usually call the equal-awakening bodhisattva — at this stage it's ultimate; one step further is buddhahood.
